unclustered.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. However, training on untrusted data can severely undermine their ability to refuse harmful requests. Notably, we find that models comply with harmful requests even though harmfulness information remains highly decodable from their internal representations. Moreover, an initial preference for refusal does not necessarily translate into sustained refusal behavior throughout generation. Together, these findings reveal a critical gap between recognizing harmful requests and consistently refusing to fulfill them. To address this gap, we introduce SAFEHOLD, a novel provider-enforced defense framework that preserves safety alignment during harmful fine-tuning by treating refusal as a sustained generation process rather than a single response decision. Specifically, SAFEHOLD preserves the aligned model's full-vocabulary response distribution at the initi
unclustered.headline: New Defense Protects Code AI Models During Fine-Tuning

unclustered.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. We propose training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier sequential triage protocol. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. Calibration freezes a nominal top-50% threshold, selecting single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers by whether the one-sided 95% Wilson lower confidence bound of pass rate among accepted cases meets the 95% clinical target line. Across 1,605 MIRA-v2, CDM, VivaBench, and in-hospital liver malignancy primary cohort cases, MIRA-v2 single-run top-50% pass rate reached 98.91%, matching five-run consistency, saving ~80% comp
unclustered.headline: New Method Improves AI Diagnosis Confidence in Clinics

unclustered.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmarks guide model selection, post-training rewards and claims of progress in artificial intelligence, yet leaderboards report aggregate scores without verifying whether each task's prompt, environment and grader agree on what counts as success. How often that agreement fails in contemporary evaluations, and in which direction confirmed defects move scores, has remained unmeasured across grading designs. Here we synthesize task-level quality reviews of 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations spanning closed-form question answering, document rubrics and agentic execution to assess whether prompts, environments and graders align. Task validity stratifies sharply by grading architecture. Closed-form benchmarks revised after public error reporting reach 92.5% verified validity, compared with 29.3% across six multi-step suites that nevertheless already supply 161 verified complex tasks. unclustered.headline: Study Questions Reliability of AI Benchmark Scores

unclustered.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. We introduce EcomWriteBench, a real-world benchmark containing 3,861 queries from 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages. Through task-level extraction, cross-task consolidation, and refinement guided by human feedback, EcomWriteBench constructs a shared pool of 37 abilities and identifies the subset applicable to each task. Ability-wise scoring enables us to compare state-of-the-art LLMs on EcomWriteBench and characterize their relative strengths and weaknesses across fine-grained e-commerce writing abilities. We further propose a preference-calib
unclustered.headline: New Benchmark Tests LLMs on Real E-commerce Writing Tasks

unclustered.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). We introduce GenAI4SimPy, a multi-agent framework powered by Qwen 3.6 (27B), an open-weight large language model, that automates end-to-end DES generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy models through tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. Evaluated on three execution blocks from a public smart factory dataset, the framework achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 7.9\% and coverage of failure rate for all three blocks and of throughput for two of three. A fidelity paradox was observed: accurate process-level parameters did not ensure system-level behavioral fidelity, with flow-time and throughput errors driven by misinterpreted observation-window truncation and absent system-level calibration. These results demonstrate that local open-weight models can perform DES generation at accu
unclustered.headline: AI Agents Generate Manufacturing Simulations for SMEs

unclustered.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. AI presence increased global diversity of human-authored ideas, but only a second AI increased within-session differentiation. The number of AI partners and their formation can reshape what the h
unclustered.headline: Study: Adding More AI Agents Doesn't Always Help Brainstorming

unclustered.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) optimises for producing the correct call, but never contrasts it with a plausible incorrect one. In an environment where even a minor formatting error can invalidate a call and an incorrect decision can derail the interaction, direct preference optimisation (DPO) targets exactly this contrast. DPO, therefore, requires preference pairs rather than plain demonstrations. For tool-calling, such data, especially in realistic multi-turn settings, remains extremely scarce. To address this scarcity, we introduce TOUMAII, a large-scale tool-calling preference dataset containing ~4.5M validated preference pairs, derived from Agent-Ark/Toucan-1.5M (apache-2.0) conversations. The dataset consists of multi- and single-turn interactions and i
unclustered.headline: TOUMAII: 4.5M Training Pairs for Tool-Calling AI Agents

unclustered.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulation and visualization scripts before execution; a high-performance computing agent dispatches jobs to remote resources; and an analysis agent interprets the completed run. The work- flow is accessible
unclustered.headline: ChatAtom: Multi-Agent LLM for Molecular Dynamics Simulation

unclustered.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards only the final answer and leaves the reasoning unverified. Same-section H&E and mIF provide what both gaps lack: mIF measures every cell without manual annotation, which gives cell-level ground truth for each step that clinical guidelines prescribe, from delineating a tissue compartment to counting and normalizing the marker-positive cells within it. unclustered.headline: AI Model Reasons Through Tumor Immune Microenvironments

unclustered.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows, these basins shrink, and spurious states emerge as attractors that blend stored samples yet match none of them. They are the first signs of generative capability. unclustered.headline: New Theory Links Memory and Generalization in AI Models

unclustered.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, where they must distinguish between normative reasoning (what should happen) and descriptive reasoning (what is likely to happen). Most fairness benchmarks evaluate demographic discrimination under a single reasoning objective, and none we know of tests whether a model treats the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. We introduce normative--descriptive calibration, the extent to which a model's differentiation between matched candidates depends on whether it is asked to predict or to decide, and measure it with the Normative--Descriptive Calibration Benchmark (NDCB): 697 matched-pair scenarios across six domains, each posed under both framings, and three metrics, Normative Engagement Rate (NER), Normative Leakage Rate (NLR), and Normative--Descriptive Separation (NDS). Across six LLMs, NDS separates 13 of 15 mode
unclustered.headline: Benchmark Tests LLMs on Normative vs Descriptive Reasoning

unclustered.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial-edit deepfake localization aims to identify manipulated regions within otherwise authentic speech. Recent systems report strong overall results, but aggregate scores do not reveal whether this performance holds across different editing conditions. In this work, we present an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL) using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on the VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit. We categorize edits along three transcript-derived axes, namely content, meaning change, and editing operation, and evaluate each generator separately. While both representations achieve strong overall performance, localization is noticeably weaker on SSR-Speech. From our experiments, we found that the deletion is the hardest operation, and deletions produced by SSR-Speech are the most challenging condition for both representations. unclustered.headline: New Method Improves Partial Deepfake Detection

unclustered.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available. The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. Early decisions mainly determine which solver should handle an untried subgoal, while later decisions determine which previously attempted subgoals should receive additional computation. unclustered.headline: Budget-Aware System Optimizes LLM Theorem Proving

unclustered.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's knowledge carries over, and progress is gated by knowledge. After every episode, we measure the places reached and ship-log rumor facts revealed, the correctness of answers to 164 questions about the
unclustered.headline: AstronautBench: New Benchmark for Self-Improving AI Agents

unclustered.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking, then adds governed cross-task self-evolution. Beyond solving individual tasks, ZhuLong-SE distills past execution traces into a three-tier memory store governed by ground-truth anchoring, disconfirmation filtering, held-out rollback, and anti-leakage retrieval. On the 158-task EDA-Eval-PyAether benchmark, the full task-level harness, with self-evolution disabled, achi
unclustered.headline: Self-Evolving AI Tackles Electronic Design Automation

unclustered.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can be tracked. We introduce CodeReviewBench, built on a fundamentally different signal: revealed developer preferences -- if a developer acts on a bot's suggestion, we treat it as useful; if they ignore it, we do not. This signal is mined daily from the public GitHub event stream, yielding 500K+ judged PRs across 18 tools, and refreshes continuously as tools evolve. We validate the developer preferenc
unclustered.headline: CodeReviewBench: Automated Testing for AI-Generated Code

unclustered.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 process-termination/restart episodes, 19,000 timed calls across 19 configurations, five targeted mutations over 43 fixtures, and 160 substitution records. No language model or autonomous agent is evaluated. OPCP and a conservative composition agree on all measured fault outcomes. Both recover after definite refusal without cross-supplier duplication; retry-all duplicates effects in every tested lost
unclustered.headline: Runtime Governance Framework for Tool-Using AI Agents

unclustered.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-4-bit quantization allows mobile devices to run larger LLMs, but its memory savings do not always translate into faster decoding on mobile NPUs. Their matrix units support only a few native integer datatypes, and converting unsupported weight formats on the vector unit can erase the gains from fewer bits. Mixed precision faces an additional constraint: each matrix-unit tile uses one datatype. MixFold executes 3-bit and perfectly symmetric 2-bit weights using native integer operations without expanding the weights to wider datatypes during decoding. MixFold then assigns datatypes to output-channel groups aligned with the matrix-unit tiles, enabling finer-than-layer assignment without disrupting matrix-unit execution. We compare MixFold with llama.cpp Hexagon backend on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU of a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Across the Qwen3 model family, MixFold achieves comparable or higher accuracy than llama.cpp's sub-4-bit formats
unclustered.headline: MixFold Accelerates Sub-4-Bit LLMs on Mobile Devices

unclustered.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.26998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reward fidelity in an adversarial reinforcement-learning loop for red-teaming financial-services language-model guardrails. Apparent wins can arise when an attack omits prescribed personally identifiable information (PII), or when a reward judge credits a response that did not break the targeted policy. On attacker-generated and public benchmark examples, TypeSafe Jev checks whether the prescribed PII is present. For outcome scoring, we compare the decision models TypeSafe Jev, Laya (pretrained and post-trained), and pretrained CLM-8B with logged Opus 4.8 judgements from a replay corpus. Post-training markedly improves Laya's agreement with the judge. A separate author-reviewed off-target set establishes that Opus can award false wins. The findings motivate specialised decision-model judges for checking prescribed PII in attack inputs and scoring target responses against the intended policy.
unclustered.headline: Reward Integrity Issues in LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming

unclustered.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. Applied to 436 BMJ Best Practice clinical monographs (354 US, 82 International), this yields 3,200 scenarios spanning differential diagnosis, investigations, treatment, and complications, plus targeted suites for regional specificity (731 US/International pairs) and temporal freshness (630 scenarios). To grade responses, we develop a clinician-calib
unclustered.headline: Evidence-Based Framework for Evaluating Medical AI

unclustered.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has become a core technique for post-training large language models, enabling students to learn from dense token-level supervision on their own generations. However, even with a capable teacher, OPD training can be unstable, leading to excessive response length, repetitive generation, and severe performance degradation. One example is \textit{spurious agreement}, where the student maintains high overlap with the teacher at the states visited but produces repetitive generations. Although such failures have been observed, the mechanisms behind these failures remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we investigate OPD through the lens of learning dynamics, tracing three mechanisms from local analysis to subsequent on-policy sampling. We first identify states where sampled-token OPD updates fail to correct teacher--student mismatch and characterize them using the student's mass on the teacher's top-$p$ set.
unclustered.headline: Study Reveals When On-Policy Distillation Fails

unclustered.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A visual agent acts on what it sees: it taps and types on a screen, or points on a camera image to show a robot where to act. One wrong step can fail its task, yet the right action is often among its own samples, passed over by its greedy decode. Choosing it is a visual judgment, since an action is best judged where it acts, not by its text or coordinates alone: as text, a tap is two numbers; drawn on the screen, it is the Post button of an empty draft. We find that this is decisive: given the screenshot and a tap's coordinates, a decision model chooses among GUI-R1-3B's samples significantly worse on average than when the tap is drawn where it lands. Bel turns this finding into a method that trains nothing and needs only a frozen policy's samples and an image on which each action can be drawn. It marks each candidate on its own copy of the image it acts on, asks a decision model for the probability that executing it is the right decision
unclustered.headline: Bel Improves Visual Agents Without Retraining

unclustered.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $\gamma$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. BenchForge grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators, defining task goals while preserving agents' choice of valid solutions. An agentic collection harness further enables agents to produce demonstrations by carrying out contact-rich interactions through sustained control and physical feedback. Assisted reference
unclustered.headline: Gamma-Scape Platform Advances Mobile Robot Intelligence

unclustered.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GraphRAG combines a language model's parametric knowledge with retrieved graph evidence, yet aggregate accuracy cannot show whether failures stem from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World action models (WAMs) exhibit strong manipulation capabilities yet often fail to follow test-time language instructions. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), widely regarded as the third generation of neural networks, represent a promising neuromorphic computing paradigm with the potential to reduce the energy footprint of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Their en-ergy efficiency makes SNNs particularly attractive for resource-constrained Edge AI devices, motivating growing research interest in Federated Learning (FL) with SNNs. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.27710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offline chain-of-thought (CoT) compression creates shorter supervision for efficient reasoning, but per-example compressors repeatedly process similar expressions across traces, wasting compressor budget. We introduce CRAFT, which abstracts problem-specific details into slots to uncover partially lexicalized expression templates (PLETs) and clusters wording variants into families. Compressing each family representative once yields shared deletion or rewriting edits, which are applied with each occurrence's own details to construct compact, ordinary-text training targets.
